sections.heading: Autonomy for teams
sections.content: The ideal product owner is fully autonomous and can build the roadmap they believe in. If challenged, they should be able to explain the reasoning behind their decisions; even if metrics are not there yet, they can retain leadership’s trust to continue. Zlokazov says giving teams autonomy, rather than having founders involved in everything, helps Revolut build more and supports growth.

sections.heading: Oversight without routine micromanagement
sections.content: Founders maintain a full overview and review every screen that ships. Product owners also present weekly progress directly to the CEO and CTO and receive steering. Zlokazov characterizes these reviews as a “last line of control” to check that products make sense and are thoroughly considered—not as micromanagement. Leaders can intervene when necessary.

sections.heading: Autonomy enables scale
sections.content: Product owners are meant to be fully autonomous and own what they build. They may be challenged, but if they can explain the reasoning behind their decisions and roadmap, they can retain leadership’s trust—even if the metrics are not there yet. Dmitry says this approach lets Revolut build many products without founders having to cut work down or micromanage every team.

sections.content: Leadership keeps a direct view of the work and intervenes if necessary. Dmitry describes going deeply into roughly 7–10 especially impactful projects, while weekly product reviews let teams present progress and receive founder steering. Founders also review every screen before it ships; he characterizes reviews as a last line of control to ensure the work makes sense and is thought through, rather than micromanagement.

answer.summary: Revolut aims to give product teams broad autonomy while keeping leadership accountable for direction and quality through selective deep dives, weekly reviews, and founders’ review of every shipped screen—not continuous micromanagement.

sections.heading: Autonomy with accountability
sections.content: Product owners are meant to be fully autonomous in deciding what to build. They may be challenged, but can explain the reasoning behind their decisions and roadmap; even if metrics have not arrived yet, sound reasoning can earn them trust to continue. Teams present weekly progress in product reviews, which Dmitry described as a final check that the work makes sense and is valuable—not micromanagement.

sections.heading: Oversight is deep but selective
sections.content: Leadership does not track every project in equal detail: Dmitry said he goes very deep on roughly 7–10 of the most impactful projects, out of a workload he described as closer to 100. Meanwhile, founders have an overview of everything and review 100% of screens before they ship; they can steer or intervene when needed. The balance lets teams build many products without requiring founders to manage every detail of every effort.
